title: Callender's 1948 San Francisco band with two basses and Mingus
summary: At the Beige Room he hired Mingus and ran a six-piece band with Teddy Edwards, with two basses.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Unless there's some particular recollection you have that might be of interest.
Well, there's many, many things. I had a band in San Francisco, and Mingus came to town so I hired him to play with my band. We had two basses. I might have mentioned that before.
I was going to ask you about that.

We played at a place called the Beige Room, on Powell, I think, in San Francisco. I loved it, but naturally they didn't understand what we were trying to do, whoever heard the two basses in the band. But since then Duke's had two basses in his band, and Charlie Barnet had two basses in his band... Maybe Duke had two before this, because this was in 1948 I'm talking about.
Duke had two basses right before Blanton came in, didn't he?
Right. Well, this was one of the times I had come back from Honolulu. I thought I'd come back and
live in the States again. So I stayed a few months. That's when I had the band in San Francisco.
Who else was in that band?

Teddy Edwards, Warren Bracken on piano, Bill Douglas I think was on drums in that band, and I had a trumpet player, Eddie...I can't think of his name at the moment either... Anyhow, I think there was about a six-piece band with two basses, which may have been ridiculous, but I liked it.
I wish I could have heard it.
Well, I say, some of the most interesting things have never been recorded, and that was one of those times.
1948. I was living in Honolulu, but I came back for some reason.
Well, you came down to L.A. at some point around that time.
